html:
The Kawaiisu are an Indigenous people of California who live in the Tehachapi Valley and north across the Tehachapi Pass in the southern Sierra Nevada, toward Lake Isabella. They speak a Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family, close to that of the Southern Paiute and the Chemehuevi.

They gathered acorns and pine nuts, hunted deer and rabbits, and wintered in villages of brush houses. Their territory linked the Central Valley to the Mojave Desert, and they traded with the Yokuts, the Tübatulabal and the Kitanemuk. Their rock paintings survive in many shelters.

After the Gold Rush, ranches, mines and the railway over Tehachapi Pass took much of their land. A winter village site is now protected as Tomo-Kahni State Historic Park.
